0.content:
Long before the Archon War, as a moon envoy, Zibai befriended a man of striking looks and impossible power who was not an angel. Once, when they had arranged to duel in the Adeptus Arts, she found him split into three identical figures fighting in the clouds, crying "The Lord of Geo, Heaven's Star!" He taught her the Three Deadly Selves art, which she could not then perform because she had no impure thoughts. He told her "The will of heaven shifts and does not stay." Later Rex Lapis freed her Third Self from a painting and made a contract with her; for ages he performed a Moonchase Rite to reach her imprisoned First Self. In 6.3 he planned her revival, hunted Ziqiao down himself and bargained her into a day in Liyue Harbor.

Now she sees him in the streets with Director Hu or sipping tea alone, and judges his consultant's life "far more pleasant and relaxed than his life as Rex Lapis". She teases him and nearly blows his cover in public, then introduces him as the funeral parlour's learned consultant. She thinks time has changed even him: "Even Rex Lapis, having waded through the waters of the river of time, is not quite the same as before."

He keeps asking to borrow her silk landscape painting; she keeps refusing because it is unfinished. Zhongli overspent the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's yearly budget on the jade token that led to her, so he is only allowed discounted tea; Zibai shops for it. When Xiao asked about Zhongli's past, she said only that in days of yore he was "the Lord of Geo, Heaven's Star", and that Xiao should ask him.

1.comment: Zibai: The Three Deadly Selves (Ziju, Zizhi, Ziqiao)
1.content:
The Three Deadly Selves art severs a practitioner's impure "selves" to reveal the pure self. At Zibai's death she severed hers, and Istaroth placed the shards of her soul inside them. Ziju, the First Self, held the Heavenly Soul (Taiguang), closest to her true nature, and was imprisoned in the false moon. Zizhi, the Second, held the Earth Soul (Shuangling), inherited most of her memories and wisdom, and slept beneath The Chasm as the embodiment of her wrath. Ziqiao, the Third, held the Human Soul (Youjing), the most free-spirited, and was sealed in a painting until Rex Lapis freed her. Restored, Zibai still shifts between them: blue eyes for Ziju, red for Zizhi, gold for Ziqiao and her usual self.

In the 6.3 Lantern Rite, Ziju met the Traveler through a broken jade token and guided them out of her prison, saying her time was nearly up. Zizhi possessed people and finally tested the Traveler with a flight from the river of time, then showed them Lang-Gan's end and gave up her fragment once her rage was stilled. Ziqiao insisted she was not Zibai at all, demanded a "contract" from Zhongli, spent a day touring Liyue Harbor with her new "guides", and then let her fragment go. On the night of Lantern Rite the wishes broke the shadowmoon and the three became one again.

Ziqiao's parting words were that "one need not fear that life is but a journey of goodbyes." Zizhi's were a couplet about a lone moon reclaiming its light. Ziju, alone for ages, counted numbers (apparently primes) in the void to remember she existed: "Even if I forget my name, I won't forget that I exist."

2.content:
An ancient kingdom of Sand Crystals and gemstones in the unified civilization, "a resplendent pearl" under Zibai's guidance. She taught its people to till and weave, and they worshipped her as the God of Soil and Grain. She says the harvests were their own work. Most of her time went to teaching children reading, arithmetic and music and compiling texts on etiquette and music. At festivals they brewed grain wine and offered it to her under the moon. When it fell, she led its survivors east; the ruins lie where The Chasm is now, and Liyue keeps unearthing its relics.

Chiwang Terrace reminded Zizhi of the altar where Lang-Gan honoured Zibai. A celadon-jade carriage and a set of ceremonial jades from the Chasm, along with the silk painting of Zhanzhu, are among the relics tied to her. The poem "Odes of Lang: Zibai" blesses crops, cloth and divination plants under the Eternal, Iridescent and Frost Moons.

Zibai says modern Liyue worships a new god and has transformed the lantern rites, yet Lang-Gan "did not perish": its people "took root in the soil of their homeland". She now teaches at Liyue schools partly so she can correct the historical record on Lang-Gan.

3.content:
The Shade of Time placed a moon crest before Zibai, making her an envoy of the moons as well as of heaven; she did not at first accept it. When the War of Funerary Flame tainted Lang-Gan, Istaroth told her it would be purified, that she was only an emissary and should feel no guilt, "and no place for hope". Zibai chose to die among her people. Istaroth sighed, "You have done enough," and froze the instant of her death, preserving her soul in her three selves.

Zizhi called that power "a blessing and a prison, all at once". Zibai's Character Stories leave Istaroth's reasons open: pity, or punishment for betrayal. They also ask whether her return was foreseen. Zhongli told the Traveler only that "the avatar of Time" had preserved her.

4.comment: Zibai: The Traveler and Paimon ("my dutiful guides")
4.content:
Zhongli "sold" the Traveler and Paimon to Ziqiao as guides for a day in Liyue Harbor, and the name stuck. On waking, Zibai first mistook the Traveler for someone her selves had possessed, then remembered "that impudent blond youngster who kept meddling in my affairs". She toured Chenyu Vale with them, cooked for them and calls them her guides with real affection. She says it is she who is in their debt for waking her.

Her friendship voice lines encourage the Traveler in their search for their kin: as a long-time resident of the moon, her blessing should "count for more than most". She repaired the broken jade token they returned into a teleporting jade chariot for their travels. When she learned they were bound for Snezhnaya she said that if they need help, they know where to find her.

5.content:
When war erupted above the skies, its fallout, laden with Abyssal malice, crashed over Lang-Gan, and the heavens resolved to purge the taint whatever the cost. Zibai defied that will and held off the strike long enough for many to escape; her spirit was "sundered into three". Zizhi's lasting regret was that with a little more time, everyone could have survived.

The vision Zizhi showed the Traveler opens with a Trilunar Syzygy as Lang-Gan gathers to honour her. Zizhi still wishes she could "burn a hole through the heavens themselves".

6.comment: Zibai: Ziqiao, the Eight Adepts and Tao Dou
6.content:
The "White Horse" an elder of Qingce Village said assisted the Lord of Geo, the "Daughter of Time" of Chenyu Vale's clans, the "Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare" in The Sanctification of Tao Dou and the horse that "leapt across the chasm of five hundred years" in the Lu clan's genealogy were all Ziqiao. Zibai says the Mare had little to do with the other Eight Adepts outside the Tao Dou incident. Several tried to catch her afterwards, "but four legs will always outrun two".

Carefree and fond of showing off, Ziqiao would help mortals in trouble while slipping them ancient stories, and ignore any written version she disliked. The wandering Wind Reader nicknamed her "White Foal" almost as soon as they met. She could not stay long near Rex Lapis because the traces of time on her hurt him.

7.content:
The false moon that hung in the sky for thousands of years, a projection of the moon, was also Ziju's prison; over countless years the two merged. When the Traveler brought back the Frost Moon, the shadowmoon began to fall apart in bursts that looked like a strange eclipse, apparently triggered by wishes. Zhongli feared Zibai would vanish with it, so he timed her rescue to Lantern Rite, when the Xiao Lanterns' wishes would break it open.

Inside, time slowed so that a mortal day felt like a century. "At least it's not as cold as on the moon," she says when it snows; at the 7.1 Moonchase she called life among mortals "better this than that cold, lonely eternity up on the moon".

8.comment: Zibai: The Lu Clan and the Baiju Guesthouse
8.content: Ziqiao once met a girl of the Lu clan in a bamboo forest and told her history as a story; the meeting entered the Lu family records. Her descendant Lu Weng runs the Baiju Guesthouse, built in the White Horse's name, and gave Zibai a long-term room and free Sunglo Tea. His granddaughter Lu Xiangxiang was possessed by Zizhi in 6.3. Xiangxiang is a restless heiress who tries archaeology, martial arts and more. Ziqiao told her to pursue whatever brings her delight. Later Zibai secretly swapped a mature tea tree into her punishment seedling's place so she would be free to choose her path.

9.content:
Zibai's great hobby is mathematics. She calls it "the foundation of all things" and wonders aloud why one plus one makes two. She and Xianyun argue pure versus applied maths: Xianyun wants practical mechanisms, and Zibai says that reduces maths to tools and destroys its beauty. After her explanation Xianyun came round to theoretical study, and they once talked until midnight. Xianyun complains that Zibai visits too often and pursues Yaoyao with worksheets.

She once visited Sumeru's Rtawahist Darshan in her wanderings, gained much from reading a few of their books, and intends to apply to the Akademiya to study further, sure that it upholds "education for all". She drew Xianyun ancient Lang-Gan mechanism blueprints, though she doubts they are still useful.

10.comment: Zibai: Moon Envoys and the Moon Wheel
10.content:
"Moon envoy" is a job title, Zibai explains: any angel, or non-angel, can hold it. Through Istaroth's crest she became one and travelled by the lunar chariot between the morning stars (heaven), the moons and Lang-Gan. The same crest is her Moon Wheel today. She remembers a colleague who liked the form of an ibis. In Nod-Krai's books, a divine envoy who once lived on the moon is still recorded.

Her Moon Wheel story calls heaven's will a light that scorches without caring and the moons' a cool light that consoles what has been burned. At Lang-Gan's end the crest she had refused "dropped onto her back like a falling tear". She remembers the Three Moon sisters as close and fond of swapping shifts.

11.comment: Zibai: The Moonchase Rite and Wind Reader
11.content:
During the 7.1 Moonchase Festival (the limited-time event Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon), Zibai revealed that the festival grew from a "Moonchase Rite" Rex Lapis performed to awaken her, later imitated by the people. When Lan Yan brought her clan's ancestor ("Grandmaster") Wind Reader ("Mad Lan"), one of the Eight Adepts, now a remnant soul under his own Soul-Binding seal, Zibai recognised the art and his "scheming". She refused to break the seal by force and helped seek the true meaning of his "Moonchase".

She found him a vulgarian and a buffoon "to the very end", then admitted he was "perhaps a rare sort of man". At the adepti's tea on Mt. Aocang she knew only that the Jade-Plumed Silverwing had once roamed with him. Learning how Silverwing's story ended, she wondered if this was what "time" truly means in the mortal realm.

12.comment: Zibai: Qiqi and the Soul-Stilling Sigil
12.content: In her anecdote Zibai waited for a private moment with Qiqi and recognised the sigil on her head as Three Deadly Selves spellwork. Only one damaged Self remains in Qiqi, reassembled by someone's intricate art and stilled by the sigil. Fetor Qiqi breathed in during an earlier adventure with the Traveler has drained the sigil to barely a tenth of its power. Zibai noticed Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver arriving in human form at Bubu Pharmacy and set out to consult them. She does not pry into what happened to Qiqi.

13.content: Freshly revived and short-tempered, Zibai mistook Shenhe for the "Crane Adeptus who loves planting Mint" and scolded her. Once calm, she apologised and sensed the dark forces bound by Shenhe's red ropes. She advised loosening one or two of them in training: external aids should give way to inner restraint. Shenhe said her master had told her the same.

key: Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame
14.comment: Zibai: Hu Tao and the Wuwang Kid
14.content: At Wuwang Hill Zibai recognised Hu Tao as heir to the Wuwang Kid or the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame, figures she remembers from the Tao Dou era. She remembers the Wuwang Kid and the Yunlai Angler pairing Glaze Lily petals with wine and drunkenly improvising sword routines. She praises Hu Tao's courage in facing death to protect others, and is relieved that the Traveler's help kept her from the Lone Butterfly's fate.

key: That Which Has Lost Its Power
15.comment: Zibai: Flavor of Spring and the Jade-Token Chariot
15.content: At Wangshu Inn Zibai suddenly remembered Flavor of Spring, served in every Lang-Gan household at the start of spring and at a feast Morax once attended. She cooked it for the Traveler, Paimon and Xiao. When the Traveler showed her the broken jade token that had linked them to Ziju, she called it a former adeptal treasure and said broken jade cannot be made whole. Later she restored it at Yilong Dais, the Gate of Life among Liyue's eight ley-line gates, and turned it into a parasol that becomes a teleporting jade chariot: her gift to her guides.

16.content: Zibai is an angel, one of the race made to guide humanity in the age of the unified civilization. Fellow angel Nicole admits she would rather not meet her. The older angels kept talking about the exceptional young woman from the neighbouring area with ties to the Archangel, and Nicole felt like a weak student next to the top of the class. Zibai's last Character Story asks whether her return has become "the true reality beheld by the first angel".
